newsitem.title: USA: Pakistan to import more wheat-U.S. ag attache.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to import more wheat-U.S. ag attache.

text.p: Pakistan plans to import more wheat than in the 1995/96 marketing year but strained port facilities will limit imports to 2.3 million tonnes, the U.S. agricultural attache in Islamabad said in a report released Monday.
The government has set a target of 2.4 million tonnes, well above an earlier plan for 1.8 million tonnes. In 1995/96, imports totaled 2.1 million tonnes.
Plans were revised because of a slight downturn in Pakistan's crop to 16.9 million tonnes, down 100,000, and requests from provinces for 2.6 million tonnes.
The United States was forecast to provide about 2 million tonnes of the imports.
When the report was written in late November, Pakistan had imported 1.035 million tonnes and a December 1 tender for 225,000 tonnes had been announced. Shipment is by month's end.
Logistical problems could impede shipment of the remaining 1.1 million tonnes, the attache wrote, because port facilities also would be handling the arrival of fertilizer cargoes.

Therefore, the report estimates that the actual imports of the Government of Pakistan (GOP) will be about 2.3 million tonnes, including the estimated arrivals of 50,000 tonnes for Afghan refugees under the World Food Program," the report said.

"Post is closely monitoring and coordinating with the GOP wheat import plan. This year monitoring is more critical to ensure on time availability of GSM-102 funds, ensure the fair competition and transparency in buying process, and maintain our competitive position."
